knowledge:
- key_parameters: IsBed=Set to FALSE for 6-column ChIA-PET tool format, TRUE for 4-column BED format with specific ID patterns (PET#\d+\.1 and PET#\d+\.2) ;; ppiType=Type of background PPI, e.g., "HPRD" or "Biogrid" ;; filter=If TRUE, filters PPI to keep only proteins in the nucleus (default GO term "GO:0005634") ;; minFreq=Minimum frequency threshold to remove rare edges (default 0.25) ;; maxFreq=Maximum frequency threshold to remove too frequent edges (default 0.75) ;; thr=Threshold to select top edges that capture thr% of the network ;; eta=HDP algorithm parameter controlling sparsity of edge-to-CMN matrix ;; gamma=HDP algorithm parameter controlling the number of CMNs ;; alpha=HDP algorithm parameter controlling sparsity of edge-to-CMN matrix ;; method=Clustering method (e.g., "sota") ;; nbClus=Number of clusters for clustering DNA interactions ;; type=Type of plot in plot3CPETRes, e.g., "heatmap", "curve", "avgCurve", "networks", "netSim"
- alternatives: The documentation mentions using ChIP-Seq directly to find proteins at loop borders, but notes limitations (not all proteins captured, lack of specific antibodies), making R3CPET's computational inference a preferred alternative. Built-in PPI networks include "HPRD" and "Biogrid", but custom PPI can be loaded via customPPI as an ncol file or igraph object.
- when_to_use: Appropriate when you have ChIA-PET interaction data and TFBS (ChIP-Seq peaks or motifs) and want to infer the specific protein complexes/networks maintaining those chromatin loops.
- pitfalls: If using a 4-column BED file for PETs, the IDs in the fourth column must strictly follow the pattern PET#\d+\.1 for the left side and PET#\d+\.2 for the right side; otherwise, an error is raised if the number of left and right side interactions differs. GenerateNetworks must be called on the HLDA result before accessing or plotting networks, as igraph networks are not created by default.

workflows.name: chromatin_maintainer_network_inference
workflows.intent: Infer and analyze the protein networks that maintain chromatin interactions using ChIA-PET, TFBS, and PPI data.
input: HepG2_interactions.txt (ChIA-PET interactions file, 6-column or 4-column BED format)
RPKMS (optional gene expression data frame for annotation/filtering)
workflows.stages: 1. Initialize the ChiapetExperimentData object with ChIA-PET and TFBS files ;; 2. Load PET interactions using loadPETs ;; 3. Load TFBS data using loadTFBS ;; 4. Load and filter the background PPI network using loadPPI ;; 5. Create indexes for processing using createIndexes ;; 6. Build protein interaction networks for each chromatin loop using buildNetworks ;; 7. Infer chromatin maintainer networks using the HLDA algorithm with InferNetworks ;; 8. Convert top edges to igraph networks using GenerateNetworks ;; 9. Annotate network proteins with gene expression using annotateExpression ;; 10. Cluster DNA interactions by enrichment profile using clusterInteractions ;; 11. Visualize results (heatmaps, curves, networks, circos) using plot3CPETRes and visualizeCircos
workflows.code:
library(R3CPET)
petFile <- file.path(system.file("example",package="R3CPET"),"HepG2_interactions.txt")  
tfbsFile <- file.path(system.file("example",package="R3CPET"),"HepG2_TF.txt.gz")  
x <- ChiapetExperimentData(pet = petFile, tfbs=  tfbsFile, IsBed = FALSE, ppiType="HPRD", filter= TRUE) 
petPath <- system.file("example","HepG2_interactions.txt",package="R3CPET")
x <- loadPETs(x,petFile=petPath, IsBed=FALSE)
TFPath <- system.file("example","HepG2_TF.txt.gz",package="R3CPET")
x <- loadTFBS(x,tfbsFile=TFPath)
x <- loadPPI(x,type="HPRD", filter=TRUE)
x <- createIndexes(x)
nets <- buildNetworks(x, minFreq=0.1, maxFreq=0.9)
hlda <- InferNetworks(nets)
hlda <- GenerateNetworks(hlda)
data(RPKMS)
hlda<- annotateExpression(hlda,RPKMS)
hlda <- clusterInteractions(hlda, method="sota",nbClus=6)
getRegionsIncluster(hlda,x,cluster=3)
plot3CPETRes( hlda, type = 'heatmap')
plot3CPETRes(hlda, type = 'curve')
plot3CPETRes(hlda, type = 'avgCurve')
nets_plot <- plot3CPETRes(hlda, type = 'networks')
plot(nets_plot[[4]])
plot3CPETRes(hlda,type = 'netSim')
visualizeCircos(hlda,x, cluster = 4)
